transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2029-07-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Liam (Redwood); Carlos, Maya, Samir, Rina (NorthStar)

Summary:
Quick discovery to understand NorthStar Edge's latency and throughput targets for a streaming chat product that they plan to scale to enterprise customers. Primary questions: p95 latency SLO, concurrency, token/sec spikes, hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, data residency and SOC2. Customer wants a realistic PoC plan and cost sketch.

Topics Covered:
- Current architecture and where inference sits in their stack
- Target p95 and acceptable tail latency for streaming responses
- Concurrent user and token/sec profiles during peak events
- Fallbacks and graceful degradation strategies
- Security/compliance requirements for Private deployment
- Benchmarking plan and next steps

---- Transcript body (timestamps approximate) ----
[00:00] Jordan Meyers: Hey everybody thanks for joining, um we're hoping to get a clear picture of your p95 targets and the expected concurrency so we can propose hosted, dedicated or private options. quick intros?
[00:14] Carlos Vega: Sure, Carlos here, CTO at NorthStar Edge. we've got Maya for ML and Samir for infra, Rina on product. we're mainly here because our enterprise customers need deterministic chat latencies.
[00:25] Maya Lin: hi all, excited to go through this — we have a demo loop today and some sample traffic patterns.
[00:30] Priya Nair: Great thanks. quick clarifier: when you say "deterministic" are you aiming for 95th percentile latency or tighter?
[00:38] Carlos: ideally p95 under 250ms on streaming tokens for short prompts (20-60 tokens), but longer contexts can be 400-500ms acceptable. that's our ambition.
[00:49] Liam Ortiz: ok that's a helpful SLO. are those numbers for end-to-end user perceived latency or just model token generation?
[00:57] Rina Patel: end-to-end, so includes network and any pre/post processing.
[01:03] Priya: Understood — that matters for routing and region placement. could you give us a peak concurrency estimate and burst profile?
[01:10] Maya: baseline 300 concurrent chat sessions, spikes to 2,500 over the course of big customer events, bursts of traffic where token/sec can jump 8-10x for a few minutes.
[01:22] Samir: Our org can't tolerate >1% throttling during those events. we want graceful degradation rather than total failures.
[01:29] Jordan: Good, that paints a picture. for spikes like that we've seen customers use a mix: hosted with autoscaling for steady-state, dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput, plus a fallback lower-cost model for overflow.
[01:42] Carlos: how does prefix / kv cache help in streaming chat? we have many repeated prompts across customers.
[01:48] Priya: good question. prefix/KV cache reduces per-token compute when there's repeated context. in streaming it means subsequent tokens are faster, less compute, and you get better p95s for repeated flows. however cache hit rate depends on how similar prompts are; we typically measure cache effectiveness during PoC.
[02:05] Maya: can you run us through latency components — where should we budget the 250ms?
[02:09] Priya: sure — rough breakdown: 20-60ms network RTT (if colocated region), 30-80ms model decoding for short tokens on optimized GPUs, 50-120ms pre/post processing and orchestrator overhead depending on batching, and some queuing during bursts. the p95 sits where those add up plus tail jitter.
[02:27] Liam: also quantization and kernel selection change latency; a quantized 8-bit variant can shave CPU time but sometimes affects quality.
[02:34] Maya: quality tradeoffs are delicate for us — can't lose hallucination rate.
[02:39] Jordan: totally, and that's why we recommend evals tied to the PoC — latency vs quality matrix.
[02:45] Carlos: Data residency and SOC2 — if we go Private we need to manage KMS and audit logs. does Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
[02:52] Priya: yes, Private supports KMS integrations and audit logs. we also provide the network diagram and deployable control plane. for enterprise we can run the control plane in your VPC or an on-prem package.
[03:02] Samir: what about egress and GPU placement — we have strict egress limits and want to keep inference inside our region.
[03:09] Priya: we can pin capacity to regions, and Dedicated tiers offer region-affinity and reserved pools. for strict egress we recommend Private with customer-controlled network.
[03:17] Rina: are there benchmarks you can share for token/sec under streaming? deck link?
[03:22] Jordan: we'll share a tailored benchmark plan but rough numbers: an M60-ish infra profile with optimized kernels can do X tokens/sec; in practice we size per model. we'll attach sample spreadsheets.
[03:33] Maya: 'X' is vague — can you give an example for a 7B model and a 13B across a single A100-ish node?
[03:40] Priya: approximate: optimized 7B can hit ~1,800-2,400 tokens/sec peak on a single A100 with continuous batching; 13B is more like 800-1,200 tokens/sec. but streaming p95s depend on batching window and concurrency. these are ballpark numbers used for initial sizing.
[04:02] Carlos: So for our 2,500 spike we'll need multiple nodes or a reserved pool. what about cold-starts and warm KV caches?
[04:10] Priya: cold-starts matter for serverless-like hosted bursts. Dedicated keeps GPUs warm and you avoid cold model load latency. also we can pre-warm checkpoints and maintain a small hot cache to reduce cold-starts.
[04:21] Samir: how do you handle request routing when capacity is constrained? we don't want opaque failures.
[04:28] Liam: Redwood routing uses policy-based routing — prefer local region, fall back to lower-cost model variants or burst pool. we expose fallbacks so you can control behavior per route (fail-open vs degrade-to-summary).
[04:40] Rina: What's the typical cost delta between hosted and dedicated for predictable throughput?
[04:45] Jordan: generally hosted has higher per-token unit cost but lower ops overhead; dedicated reduces per-token compute cost once you commit, but requires a monthly reservation. we'll send an estimated TCO comparison for your traffic profile.
[04:58] Maya: for quality measurement during PoC can you support our eval harness? we have a dataset of 2k prompts and a scoring rubric.
[05:04] Priya: absolutely — we'll run your evals against model variants and quantized profiles and return per-prompt latency and quality regressions.
[05:11] Carlos: for the PoC we need a clear benchmark run: baseline traffic, 30-minute sustained spike, and a 5-minute extreme burst. can Redwood produce those runs and provide token/sec logs and p95 breakdowns?
[05:22] Priya: yes, we can simulate that. we'll need a representative prompt set and traffic pattern; we'll instrument p50/p90/p95 and per-token latencies and share raw logs.
[05:31] Samir: on security docs — can you give SOC2 report and diagram? we need them for our procurement.
[05:36] Jordan: yes, we'll share SOC2 and the typical security pack. for Private possibilities we'll include the private deployment checklist and knob list (KMS, SSO, audit retention).
[05:46] Rina: timeline — we want a pilot by late July. realistic?
[05:50] Jordan: realistic if we start this week. propose: we send benchmark plan + pricing by Thu (2029-07-11), you provide infra diagrams by Wed (2029-07-10), then PoC kickoff on 2029-07-17.
[06:02] Maya: sounds good; who will own the coordination?
[06:05] Jordan: Jordan will own commercial and coordination; Priya and Liam will run the technical PoC. Samir to provide infra details.
[06:12] Carlos: one last question — how do you measure streaming p95 if tokens flow over time?
[06:18] Priya: we measure perceived p95 as time-to-first-meaningful-token for streaming plus per-token latencies for tail analysis. we can produce a waterfall chart tying network, decode, and queuing.
[06:29] Samir: and for throttling, we'd like to auto-fallback to a lower-compute model at 95th percentile threshold rather than dropping sessions.
[06:36] Liam: that's supported — policy-driven fallback, and you can specify degrade-to-model-id and rate.
[06:41] Rina: ok great, sounds like we'll move forward.
[06:44] Jordan: excellent. recap of next steps: we'll send the benchmark plan, pricing sketch, and SOC2 + security pack; Priya will draft the benchmark scenarios; Samir will share infra docs.
[06:56] Carlos: thanks everyone. look forward to the PoC.

Notes on transcript quirks: occasional mis-recognition on model names and numbers, e.g., 'A100-ish' typed as 'A100- ish', 'KV cache' sometimes 'K V cash' in raw output. crosstalk at 04:40 when Rina and Jordan interject.

Shared artifacts referenced:
- Benchmark plan (will be shared link)

- Cost/TCO spreadsheet sample

End of transcript.
